figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: Fig. 1. (a) Top and side views of ML CrInTe2. (b) Top and side views of ML In2Se3, with arrows (P↑ and P↓) indicating the polarization direction. (c) Top and side  views of CrInTe2/In2Se3 heterostructure featuring different stacking configurations, depicting both upward (P↑) and downward (P↓) polarizations of In2Se3.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: Fig. 2. (a) Atom-resolved magnetic anisotropy energy. p-orbital-resolved magnetic anisotropy of Te2 atoms in (b) CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↑) and (c) CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓). (d)  Atomic-layer-resolved localization of DMI-associated SOC energy. p-orbital-resolved magnetic anisotropy of Te1 atoms in (e) CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↑) and (f)  CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓).

figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: Fig. 3. (a) Spin textures of CrInTe2/In2Se3 under zero field and Bz = 50 mT. (b) Relationship between the topological charge Q and the magnetic field Bz for CrInTe2/  In2Se3(P↓). (c) Phase diagrams of CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓) as a function of temperature and Bz, along with the variation of spin texture with temperature at Bz = 2.0 T. (d)  Relationship between the skyrmion radius Rx and Bz for CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓).

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.llm_description: Fig. 4. (a) The relationship between spin texture and K under magnetic fields of 0 T and 1.6 T. (b) The energy contributions of total energy from various exchange  energies in the spin Hamiltonian. (c) The contributions of Zeeman energy (EZeeman), anisotropy energy (EAni), and DMI energy (EDMI) in the spin Hamiltonian.

figures.title: Figure 5
figures.llm_description: Fig. 5. (a) The spin texture diagram of CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓) as a function of d|| and K, with J set to 9.85 meV; (b) Spin texture diagram of CrInTe2/In2Se3(P↓)  characterized by κ. The purple, orange, green, and blue lines represent κ = −10, κ = −5, κ = 5, and κ = 10, respectively.

figures.title: Figure 6
figures.llm_description: ig. 6. Motion snapshots of (a) N´eel-type skyrmion and (b) bimeron at 0 ns, 3 ns, and 6 ns. The effect of the spin transfer torque parameter u on vx (c) and vy
